note: What the Observer's harness says to its model (2026-09-28, zero domain in the harness; 2026-10-10, on the factories' harness): the code fills the holes {name}.
intention: Formulate the TWIN_FACTORY_REQUEST for the system described in the observation.
capability: Hand over the TWIN_FACTORY_REQUEST: what the twin must represent, receive, simulate, expose, and how it will be judged. It is checked before it reaches the factory; a refused request comes back with its reasons. An accepted one is written to {file}.
read: You read {read} (their answers are in the state); read nothing twice.

brief.read: Stage 1 of 5, read. The system is in the state (hypothesis: the description, the telemetry's summary, the quantities the factories share, the library's documents). Read in the library what the description leaves open: the devices' datasheets, the station's topology and metrics (library.read gives a document whole, library.facts the facts a document states by id). {read}
brief.request: Stage 4 of 5, the request. Hand over the whole TWIN_FACTORY_REQUEST with observer.submit; {attempts} attempt(s) left. {read} The facts you chose are in the state with their values (hypothesis, field "needs"): cite each in known, by its factId; a number no fact answers is missing information or an assumption, said as such.
brief.giveUp: No attempt left: {used} request(s) refused. End with task.fail, naming the reasons that still stand (lastRefusal); the work stops here, nothing else is offered.
brief.handOver: Stage 5 of 5, hand over. The request is accepted ({path}): end with task.done, it as the artifact of kind "request".
brief.needs: Stage 2 of 5, the needs. Say what the twin needs as numbers, each in words, with observer.needs: every number the request will hold (a volume, a flow between modules, what a person produces, a device's flow or efficiency). The library gives back the facts nearest each. {read}
brief.choose: Stage 3 of 5, the choice. For each need, choose with observer.choose the fact that answers it, by its id, or none: the facts the library found are in the state (hypothesis, field "needs"). Still to choose: {open}.

guard.readFirst: read first: what the description leaves open is in the library (library.read), then hand over the request
guard.accepted: the request {path} is already accepted: end with task.done
guard.noAttemptLeft: no attempt left ({used} request(s) refused): end with task.fail and the reasons that still stand
guard.needsFirst: say the needs first (observer.needs), then choose a fact for each
guard.chooseFirst: choose a fact for each need first (observer.choose); still to choose: {open}
guard.choiceMissing: no choice for {needs}: choose a fact for each need you said, or none, with why
guard.choiceUnknown: need "{need}": "{id}" is no fact of the library; choose one of the facts the library gave back for it (the state, field "needs"), or none

doneWhen.read: at least one document of the library read
doneWhen.chosen: a fact chosen for each need, or none (observer.choose)
doneWhen.accepted: the request accepted by the guard (observer.submit)
doneWhen.handedOver: handed over with task.done, the accepted file as the artifact (kind "request")

openQuestions.read: what the description leaves open, read in the library (library.read)
openQuestions.needs: what the twin needs as numbers (observer.needs)
openQuestions.choose: the fact that answers each need (observer.choose)

validate.none: no request among the claimed artifacts
validate.notAccepted: no request was accepted by the guard in this task (observer.submit)
validate.notTheFile: claimed request "{path}" is not the file the guard accepted ({accepted})

schema.factIdExample: the fact's id in the library's typed facts (library.facts, or the facts a read document lists), when the document states them: scrubber.singlePassEfficiency, never a symbol of your own
schema.known: The constants the documentation gives (a device's datasheet, the station's metrics), each with its source: the factory holds them and never fits them.

capabilities.needs: Say what the twin needs as numbers, each in words (the flow between two modules with the hatch closed, the CO2 a person produces, the volume of a module). For each, the library gives back the {n} facts nearest it, with their value, unit and document; they stay in the state (hypothesis, field "needs"). Call it again to add needs.
capabilities.choose: For each need you said, the fact that answers it, by its id (empty when none does), and why in a few words. The facts chosen, with their values, go into the state: the request cites them in known, by factId. A need no fact answers is missing information, or an assumption said as such.
